sections.means: The post's own budget lines put e-bus procurement at ₹4,391 crore, above both the demand incentives and the charging line.
sections.todo: Track the e-bus procurement line first, since the post names it as the segment whose traction-motor deadline held firm.

sections.h2: E-bus magnets and shafts slip to April 2027; the base build keeps September 2026

events: E-truck integrated motor: assembly and controller work already in force
E-bus base traction-motor build stays due as scheduled
E-bus magnet and shaft fitment due; standalone e-truck full build due

sections.means: For e-buses the base build stays due on 1 September 2026, and only the magnet and shaft fitment move to 1 April 2027.
sections.todo: Check magnet sourcing for e-bus traction motors well before 1 April 2027, since the post says that is the input industry cannot yet source domestically.

sections.h2: No magnet beneficiary was named by 7 November, with the April 2027 deadline still standing

events: China's licensing of seven heavy rare earths, including dysprosium, takes effect
Technical bids opened for the ₹7,280cr rare-earth magnet scheme, 20 in all
No beneficiary named yet; the 1 April 2027 magnet deadline stands

sections.means: The post reports 20 bids for the ₹7,280cr magnet scheme, but no beneficiary named by 7 November, so domestic magnet capacity has not started.
sections.todo: Watch for a named beneficiary under the magnet scheme as the first sign that the April 2027 magnet deadline can be met.
